subject: Re: Integration proposal — TraceStitch SDK shim + prompt-sandbox
messages:
From: Maya Patel <maya@signalforge.ai>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: TraceStitch + Redwood — quick intro and tech ask

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for taking 10 minutes on Friday. SignalForge (we spun out from FluxOps) has been working on TraceStitch, a small tracing spec and a lightweight SDK that stitches traces across toolchains and model backends. We're seeing a lot of ISVs (prompt linters, eval platforms, tracing UIs) ask for a single shim that can be added to SDKs (LangChain / LlamaIndex adapters) so traces correlate across customer environments.

We think Redwood's routing and caching make you a natural partner — specifically for:
- A small SDK shim that preserves trace IDs across redirects and proxying.
- A test harness: prompt-sandbox that runs canonical prompt sets to validate fidelity and telemetry.

Are you open to a scoped integration where SignalForge provides the TraceStitch spec + a quickstart and Redwood supplies an example LangChain adapter and a Hosted test workspace for 30 days?

Attaching a short spec and a draft mutual action plan. Proposed timing: 2-week tech spike -> 4-week pilot.

Best,
Maya Patel
Head of Integrations, SignalForge

Attachment: trace-stitch-spec-v1.pdf (application/pdf)

From: olga_petrov@redwood.ai
To: Maya Patel <maya@signalforge.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: TraceStitch + Redwood — quick intro and tech ask

Maya — thanks, this looks promising. I'm looping in Ben (ecosystem) and Karthik (integrations) to scope the engineering effort.

High-level notes:
- We like a shim approach (min surface area) that plays nicely with our routing/fallbacks.
- For hosted pilots we need clear telemetry boundaries and an opt-in flow so customers can toggle TraceStitch headers.

Ben/Karthik — can you review the spec PDF and confirm whether a LangChain adapter plus a lightweight LlamaIndex connector (both as example implementations) is feasible within a 2-week spike? Also flag any security/compliance concerns — e.g., PII in trace metadata.

Next steps:
1) Quick sync (30m) this week to align scope.
2) If green, we sign the mutual action plan and spin up a sandbox workspace.

—
Olga Petrov
Strategic Partnerships, Redwood Inference
olga_petrov@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0218

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.ai; Maya Patel <maya@signalforge.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 08:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: TraceStitch + Redwood — quick intro and tech ask

Maya / Olga — happy to jump on this. Quick engineering read:
- LangChain adapter: low effort (~3 dev days) to add TraceStitch header propagation and small helper to emit trace metadata into our request logs. We can provide an example in our SDK repo.
- LlamaIndex connector: similarly small, but we should be explicit about what fields go into the trace to avoid leaking user prompts. Recommend a default allowlist: trace_id, model_variant, prompt_template_id; prompt text must be hashed unless customer explicitly opts-in.
- Hosted sandbox: ops can spin up a time-limited workspace, but we need a signed MPA (mutual action plan) for legal and security review.

Karthik, any notes on implementation risks? Also, Maya — can you confirm the spec includes an opt-in consent flow and a small JSON schema for trace payloads?

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Ecosystem Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>; olga_petrov@redwood.ai; Maya Patel <maya@signalforge.ai>
Date: Thu, 13 May 2027 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: TraceStitch + Redwood — quick intro and tech ask

All — reviewed the spec PDF and attached the quick notes inline. Short summary:
- Implementation: we can do a minimal shim that hooks into LangChain's run flow (around run/async_run) capturing the trace_id and ensuring it flows to Redwood's routing layer. 4 APIs: init, attach_trace, record_meta, end_trace.
- Security: must avoid storing raw prompt text by default. Use one-way hashing (sha256) with a salt per customer if they opt-in to full-text tracing.
- Observability: we'll emit two counters and a histogram (trace.latency) so you can correlate prompt fidelity regressions.

I'll prepare a PR template and a test matrix for the 2-week spike. Olga — please share the MPA and we'll route to security.

-Karthik
Principal Engineer, Integrations

> On Tue, May 11, 2027 at 09:12 AM Maya Patel <maya@signalforge.ai> wrote:
> > (attached spec)

From: Maya Patel <maya@signalforge.ai>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.ai; Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>; Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 16 May 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: TraceStitch + Redwood — quick intro and tech ask

Thanks everyone — this is great. I've attached an edited mutual action plan (MPA) and a short quickstart for the prompt-sandbox. Key points from our side:
- We will provide the TraceStitch spec (final) and two reference shims (LangChain + LlamaIndex) as Apache-2.0 licensed samples.
- SignalForge will host the test harness for the first 30 days; Redwood will provide a hosted workspace + example dataset.
- Security: customers can opt-in to full traces; default will be hashed prompt text.

Next steps:
- Olga: share the MPA with legal / security for signatures (attached: sf-redwood-mutual-action-plan.xlsx).
- Karthik/Ben: tech spike backlog + quick PR template.

Looking forward — happy to demo the prompt-sandbox next week on the sync.

Best,
Maya
Head of Integrations, SignalForge

Attachments: sf-redwood-mutual-action-plan.xlsx; prompt-sandbox-quickstart.md
